## How This Was Found
While merging upstream v26.10.0 into our fork (`chore/sync-upstream-v26.10.0`), running `yarn lint` locally turned up many lint and formatting errors that were already on our `master`. That made us look into why CI hadn't caught them. We had been letting the failing CI checks through on every PR, assuming they failed because we lack access to some upstream resource. Investigating showed that the jobs never run at all: they wait for upstream's paid runner service, which we don't have access to.

## Observed Behavior (OB)
CI jobs on PRs and on `master` never start. They sit at "Waiting for a runner to pick up this job..." until GitHub cancels them. As a result, no PR has ever had working checks. Lint, typecheck, and test failures have reached `master` without being caught. `master` currently has 93 files with formatting issues and 4 lint errors.

Of the last 200 workflow runs: 133 were cancelled after queuing, 47 were skipped, and 20 are still queued (including the Test and Check runs on the `chore/sync-upstream-v26.10.0` PR, queued since 2026-10-16).

## Expected Behavior (EB)
When a PR is opened or updated, its CI jobs (Check, Test, Build, E2E) are picked up by a runner promptly, run to completion, and report a pass or fail on the PR.

## Steps to Reproduce (S2R)
1. Open a pull request against `master` (or push a new commit to an existing PR).
2. Open the PR's **Checks** tab.
3. Observe that every job stays at "Queued — Waiting for a runner to pick up this job..."
4. Come back after about 24 hours and observe that the jobs were cancelled without running.

## Additional Information
**Root cause:** Our workflows are inherited from upstream (`actualbudget/actual`) and request Depot runners, e.g. `runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest`. Depot is a paid runner service that upstream pays for. Our org has no Depot integration, so no runner ever accepts these jobs. This is a runner problem, not a missing key or secret.

Runner labels currently used across `.github/workflows/`:
- `depot-ubuntu-latest` (55), `depot-ubuntu-latest-4` (5), `depot-ubuntu-22.04` (1)
- `depot-macos-latest` (1), `depot-windows-2022` (1)
- `ubuntu-latest` (3, already GitHub-hosted)

Our repo is public, so GitHub-hosted runners are free with no minute limits.

**Proposed fix:** Replace the Depot runner labels with GitHub-hosted equivalents (`ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-22.04`, `macos-latest`, `windows-2022`), and disable the upstream-only workflows that need upstream's credentials.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. No workflow in `.github/workflows/` uses a `depot-*` runner label.
2. Opening a PR against `master` starts Check, Test, and Build jobs within a few minutes, and they report pass/fail on the PR.
3. Upstream-only workflows (nightly desktop publish, npm publish, i18n upload, stale PR cleanup, theme catalog scan) are disabled and no longer queue or fail.
4. The team knows that future upstream syncs may conflict on `runs-on:` lines, and that the resolution is to keep our GitHub-hosted runner labels.

## Out of Scope
- Fixing the existing lint and formatting errors on `master` (separate ticket). Expect the lint check to fail on the first working run until that is done.
- Making the upstream-only publishing workflows work for our fork.
- Fixing the 6 failing tests in `packages/desktop-client/src/budget/mutations.test.tsx`, which already fail on `master`.

## Open Questions
- Do we need the macOS and Windows jobs (Electron builds), or should we disable them to keep CI fast?
- Should we make the Check and Test workflows required status checks on `master`, so a failing PR can't be merged?
- Is anyone relying on any of the upstream-only scheduled workflows?

## Rough Scope
Medium
- The core fix is a find-and-replace of runner labels across the workflow files. No application code changes.
- Disabling the upstream-only workflows can be done from the GitHub Actions UI without editing files.
- Verification takes one test PR to confirm jobs get picked up and finish.
- Some uncertainty keeps this from being a 1–2: once jobs actually run for the first time, some workflows may have problems that were hidden until now. For example, E2E jobs may be slower on GitHub-hosted runners than on upstream's larger Depot machines, or a job may expect a secret or setting we don't have. Each of those is likely small, but we won't know until CI runs.
- Ongoing cost is low but not zero: each upstream sync may bring back `depot-*` labels when upstream edits a workflow, and those need to be changed back during the merge.

```text

action.yml
----
name: Setup
description: Setup the environment for the project

inputs:
  working-directory:
    description: 'Working directory to run in, default .'
    required: false
    default: '.'
  download-translations:
    description: 'Whether to download translations as part of setup, default true'
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  cache:
    description: 'Whether to restore and save dependency and Lage caches, default true'
    required: false
    default: 'true'

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Install node
      uses: actions/setup-node@53b83947a5a98c8d113130e565377fae1a50d02f # v6.3.0
      with:
        node-version: 24
        package-manager-cache: false
    - name: Install yarn
      run: npm install -g yarn
      shell: bash
      if: ${{ env.ACT }}
    - name: Get Node version
      id: get-node
      run: echo "version=$(node -v)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      shell: bash
    - name: Cache
      uses: actions/cache@cdf6c1fa76f9f475f3d7449005a359c84ca0f306 # v5.0.3
      if: ${{ inputs.cache == 'true' }}
      id: cache
      with:
        path: ${{ format('{0}/**/node_modules', inputs.working-directory) }}
        key: yarn-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.get-node.outputs.version }}-${{ hashFiles(format('{0}/**/yarn.lock', inputs.working-directory)) }}
    - name: Cache Yarn download cache
      uses: actions/cache@cdf6c1fa76f9f475f3d7449005a359c84ca0f306 # v5.0.3
      if: ${{ inputs.cache == 'true' && steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' }}
      with:
        path: ${{ format('{0}/.yarn/cache', inputs.working-directory) }}
        key: yarn-dl-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.get-node.outputs.version }}-${{ hashFiles(format('{0}/**/yarn.lock', inputs.working-directory)) }}
        restore-keys: |
          yarn-dl-${{ runner.os }}-${{ steps.get-node.outputs.version }}-
          yarn-dl-${{ runner.os }}-
    - name: Ensure Lage cache directory exists
      run: mkdir -p "$WORKING_DIRECTORY/node_modules/.cache/lage"
      shell: bash
      env:
        WORKING_DIRECTORY: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
    - name: Cache Lage
      uses: actions/cache@cdf6c1fa76f9f475f3d7449005a359c84ca0f306 # v5.0.3
      if: ${{ inputs.cache == 'true' }}
      with:
        path: ${{ format('{0}/node_modules/.cache/lage', inputs.working-directory) }}
        key: lage-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.job }}-${{ github.sha }}
        restore-keys: |
          lage-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.job }}-
    - name: Install
      working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      run: yarn --immutable
      shell: bash
      if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
    - name: Download translations
      uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
      with:
        repository: actualbudget/translations
        path: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}/packages/desktop-client/locale
        persist-credentials: false
      if: ${{ inputs.download-translations == 'true' && !env.ACT }}
    - name: Remove untranslated languages
      run: packages/desktop-client/bin/remove-untranslated-languages
      shell: bash
      if: ${{ inputs.download-translations == 'true' && !env.ACT }}
```

=== crdt-version-check
     1	name: CRDT version bump check
     2
     3	on:
     4	  pull_request:
     5	    paths:
     6	      - 'packages/crdt/**'
     7
     8	permissions:
     9	  contents: read
    10
    11	jobs:
    12	  check-version-bump:
    13	    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    14	    name: Ensure @actual-app/crdt version is bumped
    15	    steps:
    16	      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
    17	        with:
    18	          fetch-depth: 0
    19	          persist-credentials: false
    20
    21	      - name: Verify version bump
    22	        env:
    23	          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
    24	        run: |
    25	          set -euo pipefail
    26
    27	          if ! git cat-file -e "origin/${BASE_REF}:packages/crdt/package.json" 2>/dev/null; then
    28	            echo "packages/crdt/package.json does not exist on the base branch; skipping."
    29	            exit 0
    30	          fi
    31
    32	          BASE_VERSION=$(git show "origin/${BASE_REF}:packages/crdt/package.json" | jq -r .version)
    33	          HEAD_VERSION=$(jq -r .version packages/crdt/package.json)
    34	          echo "Base version: $BASE_VERSION"
    35	          echo "Head version: $HEAD_VERSION"
    36
    37	          if [ "$BASE_VERSION" = "$HEAD_VERSION" ]; then
    38	            echo "::error file=packages/crdt/package.json::Files in packages/crdt/ were modified but the @actual-app/crdt version was not bumped. Please update the \"version\" field in packages/crdt/package.json."
    39	            exit 1
    40	          fi
    41
    42	          HIGHEST=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$BASE_VERSION" "$HEAD_VERSION" | sort -V | tail -n1)
    43	          if [ "$HIGHEST" != "$HEAD_VERSION" ]; then
    44	            echo "::error file=packages/crdt/package.json::The @actual-app/crdt version ($HEAD_VERSION) must be greater than the base version ($BASE_VERSION)."
    45	            exit 1
    46	          fi
    47
    48	          echo "Version bumped from $BASE_VERSION to $HEAD_VERSION."

     1	name: VRT Comment
     4	on:
     8	  workflow_run: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
     9	    workflows: ['E2E Tests']
    10	    types:
    11	      - completed
    12
    13	permissions:
    14	  actions: read
    15	  pull-requests: write
    16
    17	jobs:
    18	  comment:
    19	    name: Post VRT Comment
    20	    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    21	    if: github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'
    22	    steps:
    23	      - name: Download VRT metadata
    24	        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
    25	        with:
    26	          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    27	          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
    28	          name: vrt-comment-metadata
    29	          path: /tmp/vrt-metadata
    30	        continue-on-error: true
    31
    32	      - name: Extract metadata
    33	        id: metadata
    34	        run: |
    35	          if [ ! -f "/tmp/vrt-metadata/pr-number.txt" ]; then
    36	            echo "No metadata found, skipping..."
    37	            echo "should_comment=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    38	            exit 0
    39	          fi
    40
    41	          PR_NUMBER=$(cat "/tmp/vrt-metadata/pr-number.txt")
    42	          VRT_RESULT=$(cat "/tmp/vrt-metadata/vrt-result.txt")
    43	          ARTIFACT_URL=$(cat "/tmp/vrt-metadata/artifact-url.txt")
    44
    45	          echo "pr_number=$PR_NUMBER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    46	          echo "vrt_result=$VRT_RESULT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    47	          echo "artifact_url=$ARTIFACT_URL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    48
    49	          if [ "$VRT_RESULT" = "failure" ]; then
    50	            echo "should_comment=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    51	            echo "VRT tests failed for PR #$PR_NUMBER"
    52	          else
    53	            echo "should_comment=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    54	            echo "VRT tests passed or skipped for PR #$PR_NUMBER"
    55	          fi
    56
    57	      - name: Comment on PR with VRT report link
    58	        if: steps.metadata.outputs.should_comment == 'true'
    59	        uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@0ea0beb66eb9baf113663a64ec522f60e49231c0 # v3.0.4
    60	        with:
    61	          number: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.pr_number }}
    62	          header: vrt-comment
    63	          hide_and_recreate: true
    64	          hide_classify: OUTDATED
    65	          message: |
    66	            <!-- vrt-comment -->
    67	            VRT tests ❌ failed. [View the test report](${{ steps.metadata.outputs.artifact_url }}).
    68
    69	            To update the VRT screenshots, comment `/update-vrt` on this PR. The VRT update operation takes about 10 to 15 minutes.

     1	name: Electron Master
     2
     3	defaults:
     4	  run:
     5	    shell: bash
     6
     7	env:
     8	  CI: true
     9
    10	on:
    11	  push:
    12	    tags:
    13	      - v**

    15	concurrency:
    16	  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

    18
    19	jobs:

    24	    steps:

    26	        id: process_version
    27	        run: |
    28	          echo "version=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    29	      - name: Create draft release
    30	        env:
    31	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    32	          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    33	          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
    34	          RELEASE_NOTES: |
    35	            :link: [View release notes](https://actualbudget.org/blog/release-${{ steps.process_version.outputs.version }})
    36
    38	            Please note: Microsoft store updates can sometimes lag behind the main release by a couple of days while they verify the new version.
    39

     1	name: Migration warnings comment
     2
    12	on:
    15	  workflow_run: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
    16	    workflows: ['Test']
    17	    types:
    18	      - completed
    19
    20	permissions: {}
    21
    22	jobs:
    23	  comment:
    24	    if: github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'
    25	    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    26	    permissions:
    27	      actions: read
    28	      pull-requests: write
    29	    steps:
    30	      - name: Download warnings artifact
    31	        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
    32	        with:
    33	          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    34	          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
    37	          pattern: migration-warnings
    38	          merge-multiple: true
    39	          path: warnings
    40
    41	      - name: Post or update PR comment
    42	        if: hashFiles('warnings/migration-warnings.json') != ''
    43	        env:
    44	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    45	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    46	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
    47	        run: |
    48	          set -euo pipefail
    49	          JSON=warnings/migration-warnings.json
    50	          MARKER='<!--- migration-warnings --->'
    51
    52	          PR=$(cat warnings/migration-warnings-pr.txt)
    53	          if ! [[ "$PR" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    54	            echo "Invalid PR number in artifact"
    55	            exit 1
    56	          fi
    57
    60	          if [ "$(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR" --jq .head.sha)" != "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
    61	            echo "Artifact PR head does not match triggering run head; skipping"
    62	            exit 0
    63	          fi
    64
    65	          existing=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/comments" --paginate \
    66	            --jq '.[] | select(.user.login == "github-actions[bot]") | select(.body | contains("<!--- migration-warnings --->")) | .id')
    67	          existing=${existing%%$'\n'*}
    68
    70	          if jq -e 'length == 0' "$JSON" > /dev/null; then
    71	            if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    72	              gh api -X DELETE "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$existing"
    73	            fi
    74	            exit 0
    75	          fi
    76
    79	          jq -e '
    80	            type == "array" and all(.[];
    81	              (.name | type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,200}$")) and
    82	              (.risks | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[];
    83	                IN("drops a table", "drops a column", "renames a table or column"))))
    84	          ' "$JSON" > /dev/null
    85
    86	          body="$MARKER
    88
    89	          $(jq -r '.[] | . as $m | .risks[] | "- `\($m.name)` \(.)."' "$JSON")
    90
    91	          Migrations must be additive-only: removing or renaming tables or columns breaks older clients that sync the same budget file. See the [migration guidelines](https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/project-details/migrations).
    92
    93	          <sub>This is an automated advisory check — it may be a false positive and does not block the PR.</sub>"
    94
    95	          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    96	            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$existing" -f body="$body"
    97	          else
    98	            gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/comments" -f body="$body"
    99	          fi

     1	name: Release notes
     2
     3	on:
     4	  pull_request:
     5	  push:
     6	    branches:
     7	      - release
     8
     9	permissions: {}
    10
    11	concurrency:
    12	  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
    13	  cancel-in-progress: true
    14
    15	jobs:
    16	  check-release-notes:
    17	    if: >-
    18	      github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    19	      && github.head_ref != 'release'
    20	      && startsWith(github.head_ref, 'release-notes/') == false
    21	      && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'
    22	    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    23	    permissions:
    24	      contents: read
    25	    steps:
    26	      - name: Check if triggered by bot
    27	        id: bot-check
    28	        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
    29	        with:
    30	          script: |
    31	            const { data: commit } = await github.rest.git.getCommit({
    32	              owner: context.repo.owner,
    33	              repo: context.repo.repo,
    34	              commit_sha: context.payload.pull_request.head.sha,
    35	            });
    36	            const skip = commit.author.name === 'github-actions[bot]'
    37	              && commit.message.startsWith('Generate release notes');
    38	            console.log(`Head commit by "${commit.author.name}": ${commit.message.split('\n')[0]}`);
    39	            console.log(`Skip: ${skip}`);
    40	            core.setOutput('skip', String(skip));
    41
    42	      - name: Checkout
    43	        if: steps.bot-check.outputs.skip != 'true'
    44	        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
    45	        with:
    46	          fetch-depth: 0
    47	          persist-credentials: false
    48
    49	      - name: Get changed files
    50	        if: steps.bot-check.outputs.skip != 'true'
    51	        id: changed-files
    52	        run: |
    53	          git fetch origin ${GITHUB_BASE_REF}
    54	          CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}...HEAD)
    55	          NON_DOCS_FILES=$(echo "$CHANGED_FILES" | grep -v -e "^packages/docs/" -e "^\.github/actions/docs-spelling/" || true)
    56
    57	          if [ -z "$NON_DOCS_FILES" ] && [ -n "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
    58	            echo "only_docs=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    59	            echo "only documentation files changed, skipping release notes check"
    60	          else
    61	            echo "only_docs=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    62	          fi
    63
    64	      - name: Check release notes
    65	        if: >-
    66	          steps.bot-check.outputs.skip != 'true'
    67	          && steps.changed-files.outputs.only_docs != 'true'
    68	        uses: ./.github/actions/release-notes/check
    69
    70	  generate-release-notes:
    71	    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    72	    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    73	    environment: release
    74	    permissions:
    75	      contents: write
    76	      pull-requests: read
    77	    steps:
    78	      - name: Resolve version
    79	        id: version
    80	        env:
    81	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    82	        run: |
    83	          version=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/contents/packages/desktop-client/package.json?ref=release" --jq '.content' | base64 -d | jq -r .version)
    84	          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    85	          echo "notes_branch=release-notes/$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    86
    90	          repo_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
    91	          if git ls-remote --exit-code "$repo_url" "refs/tags/v$version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    92	            echo "Tag v$version already published; skipping generation"
    93	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    94	          elif ! git ls-remote --exit-code "$repo_url" "refs/heads/release-notes/$version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    95	            echo "Notes branch release-notes/$version does not exist yet; skipping generation"
    96	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    97	          else
    98	            echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    99	          fi
   100
   101	      - name: Checkout release-notes branch
   102	        if: steps.version.outputs.skip != 'true'
   103	        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
   104	        with:
   105	          ref: ${{ steps.version.outputs.notes_branch }}
   106	          fetch-depth: 0
   107	          persist-credentials: true
   108
   109	      - name: Generate release notes
   110	        if: steps.version.outputs.skip != 'true'
   111	        uses: ./.github/actions/release-notes/generate
   112	        with:
   113	          release-branch: release
   114	          notes-branch: ${{ steps.version.outputs.notes_branch }}
   115	          version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}

=== workflows/issues-close-feature-requests
name: Close feature requests with automated message

on:
  issues:
    types: [typed]

permissions:
  issues: write

jobs:
  needs-votes:
    if: ${{ github.event.type.name == 'Feature' }}
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
    steps:
      - name: Add needs votes label
        run: gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --add-label "needs votes"
      - name: Add reactions
        uses: aidan-mundy/react-to-issue@109392cac5159c2df6c47c8ab3b5d6b708852fe5 # v1.1.2
        with:
          issue-number: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          reactions: '+1'
      - name: Create comment
        env:
          COMMENT_BODY: |
            :sparkles: Thanks for sharing your idea! :sparkles:

            This repository uses a voting-based system for feature requests. While enhancement issues are automatically closed, we still welcome feature requests! The voting system helps us gauge community interest in potential features. We also encourage community contributions for any feature requests marked as needing votes (just post a comment first so we can help guide you toward a successful contribution).

            The enhancement backlog can be found here: https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/issues?q=label%3A%22needs+votes%22+sort%3Areactions-%2B1-desc+

            Don't forget to upvote the top comment with 👍!

            <!-- feature-auto-close-comment -->
        run: gh issue comment "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --body "$COMMENT_BODY"
      - name: Close Issue
        run: gh issue close "$ISSUE_NUMBER"

name: Close tech support issues with automated message

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]

permissions:
  issues: write

jobs:
  tech-support:
    if: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'tech-support' }}
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Create comment and close issue
        run: |
          gh issue comment "$ISSUE_URL" --body ":wave: Thanks for reaching out!

          GitHub Issues are reserved for bug reports and feature requests, so tech support tickets are automatically closed. The fastest way to get help is to ask the community on [Discord](https://discord.gg/pRYNYr4W5A) — that's where most of the community lives and can help you in real time.

          <!-- tech-support-auto-close-comment -->"

          gh issue close "$ISSUE_URL"
        env:
          ISSUE_URL: https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/issues/${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: Remove 'help wanted' label from closed issues

on:
  issues:
    types: [closed]

permissions:
  issues: write

jobs:
  remove-help-wanted:
    if: ${{ github.event.issue.type.name != 'Feature' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'help wanted') }}
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Remove 'help wanted' label
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: gh issue edit "$ISSUE_NUMBER" --remove-label "help wanted"

## Composite actions (`/workspaces/actual-budget/.github/actions/`)

- **`setup/action.yml`**: nothing Depot-specific and no secrets. It uses Node 24, the standard `actions/cache` for `**/node_modules` (keyed by OS, Node version and `yarn.lock` hash), the yarn download cache, and a Lage cache keyed per job and SHA. Every job saves its own Lage cache, so the 10 GB repo cache limit will churn. With `download-translations` left at its default (`true`) it clones the public `actualbudget/translations` repo; build.yml `web`/`mobile`, electron-pr, electron-master and netlify-release all do this.
- **`release-notes/check` and `release-notes/generate`**: plain Node scripts using `github.token`. Nothing upstream-specific.
- **`handle-feature-requests.js`**: GraphQL queries hardcoded to `owner: "actualbudget", name: "actual"`.
- **`docs-spelling/`**: only a typos config.

## Timeouts, concurrency, sharding, machine-size assumptions

- **timeout-minutes**: none in e2e-test.yml, check.yml or build.yml, so jobs use the 360-minute default. A job stuck waiting on a Depot label sits for a long time before failing.
- **concurrency**: all three use `${workflow}-${PR number || ref}`. e2e cancels in progress always; check and build cancel except on master.
- **Sharding**: e2e `functional` and `vrt` use a fixed matrix `shard: [1, 2, 3]`. Steps run only if `matrix.shard <= vars.E2E_SHARD_TOTAL || '3'`, so the repo variable can shrink the shard count but not raise it above 3; going above 3 means editing the matrix. Each shard sets `E2E_PORT=3000+shard`. vrt-update-generate hardcodes `/3`.
- **Large-machine assumptions**:
  - `functional`, `functional-desktop-app`, api-browser-test and docker-* use `depot-ubuntu-latest-4`; electron jobs use 8-core labels.

The agent has sorted all 38 workflows. Combined with what I found directly, here's the picture before I ask you anything.

## What I found

**Root cause:** the issue has it right. Jobs request `depot-*` runners, nobody provides them, and the jobs queue until GitHub cancels them. There are three more problems the issue's proposed find-and-replace wouldn't catch:

1. **`master` would stay red even after the swap.** The Depot test-report step in [check.yml:117](.github/workflows/check.yml#L117) runs on every push to `master`, and it logs in to Depot, which we don't have.
2. **Some upstream safety switches are off for us.** Workflows like `docker-nightly`, `publish-nightly-electron` and the scheduled `publish-npm-packages` are meant to skip themselves on forks. They check `github.event.repository.fork`, and the GitHub API reports our repo as `fork: false`. So once runners work, they **will run**. For example, `docker-nightly` would build and push images to `ghcr.io/csci-435-se/...` on every merge to `master`.
3. **Some bots act on our repo or point at upstream's.**
   - [stale.yml](.github/workflows/stale.yml) would auto-close our PRs.
   - `autofix.yml` fails on every PR unless the autofix.ci GitHub App is installed.
   - `issues-close-tech-support` posts links to upstream's issues.
   - `release-notes` fails any PR that doesn't add an `upcoming-release-notes/*.md` file.

**What already works:**

- The shared [setup action](.github/actions/setup/action.yml) uses no secrets and nothing Depot-specific.
- None of the core PR workflows (Check, Build, E2E, API browser, Electron PR) need a secret beyond the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- GitHub's free Linux runners for public repos (4 cores, 16 GB) are about the size of `depot-ubuntu-latest-4`. Playwright runs inside a pinned container, so screenshot tests shouldn't drift because of the host.

## Options

**A. Swap the labels in place (the issue's proposal)**

- Replace every `depot-*` label in all workflow files with the GitHub-hosted equivalent.
- Guard the Depot report steps and the upstream-only workflows with `if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'`, which upstream already uses.
- **Pro:** every upstream improvement flows through.
- **Con:** it touches about 38 files. Upstream syncs will conflict on those lines, and new upstream jobs will quietly bring Depot labels back.

**B. Leave upstream's files alone and add our own CI file**

- Turn off every inherited workflow in the GitHub Actions settings page. That setting survives syncs.
- Add one fork-owned `fork-ci.yml` that runs lint, typecheck, tests and build on `ubuntu-latest`.
- **Pro:** upstream syncs never conflict, and CI is small, fast and easy for the team to follow.
- **Con:** we lose E2E, screenshot tests and the PR bots unless we copy them in, and nothing in the code shows that the inherited workflows are turned off.

**C. Hybrid (my recommendation)**

- Swap labels only in the core PR workflows: `check`, `build`, `e2e-test`, `api-browser-test`, and optionally `electron-pr`.
- Guard the Depot report steps.
- Turn off all the upstream release, publish and scheduled workflows in the Actions settings page, so their files stay identical to upstream.
- Add a small fork-owned `fork-ci-guard.yml` that fails if any active workflow still contains `depot-`, plus a script that re-applies the swap after each upstream sync. That covers acceptance criterion 4.
- **Pro:** about 5 files differ from upstream, upstream syncs conflict rarely, and the guard catches the quiet-regression case.

**D. A self-hosted runner, or paying for Depot**

- Run our own machine registered under the `depot-*` labels, or buy a Depot plan.
- I'd rule both out. A self-hosted runner on a public repo runs code from any PR on your machine, and GitHub explicitly warns against it. Depot costs money and adds nothing over the free runners.

I need a few decisions from you before I finish the plan.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 01:31:11Z)**_

Sure. Your answer about admin access also changes the options, so I'll explain both together.

## How GitHub CI works

1. **Workflow files.** Every YAML file in [.github/workflows/](.github/workflows/) is a recipe. Its `on:` section says when it runs (for example `pull_request:` means "whenever a PR is opened or updated"). It also lists **jobs**, and each job is a list of shell steps like `yarn lint` or `yarn test`.
2. **`runs-on:` picks the machine.** Every job has a line like `runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest`. That line is a **label**, a request for a machine of that type. GitHub puts the job in a queue and waits until a machine with that label offers to take it.
3. **Who answers which label.** GitHub's own free machines answer to labels like `ubuntu-latest`, `windows-2022` and `macos-latest`. Labels starting with `depot-` are answered only by Depot's machines, and Depot only sends machines to organizations that pay for it. Upstream pays; we don't.
4. **Why things time out.** Our jobs ask for `depot-*`, so no machine ever volunteers. They sit at "Waiting for a runner…" until GitHub gives up after about 24 hours. Nothing is broken in the tests themselves; they never got a computer to run on.
5. **Why upstream syncs matter.** When we pull in a new upstream release, git merges their changes into ours line by line. If upstream changed a line _we_ also changed, git can't decide and stops with a **merge conflict**, which someone has to fix by hand. So the more workflow lines we edit, the more hand-fixing each future sync needs.
6. **A useful detail for testing the fix.** For `pull_request` workflows, GitHub runs the workflow files _from the PR's branch_. So the PR that fixes the labels proves itself: if its checks start running, the fix works.

## What changes because you don't have admin access

My earlier Option B and Option C relied on turning off workflows from the Actions tab. In code, there are two ways to turn off a workflow:

- **Add a guard line** to each job: `if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'`. The job then reports "skipped" everywhere except upstream's repo. Upstream already uses this exact pattern in several files.
- **Delete the file.** That's simple, but whenever upstream later edits a file we deleted, git asks during the sync whether to keep it deleted. That's easy to answer, but it comes up on every sync.

You may be able to turn workflows off from the Actions tab with ordinary write access (Actions tab → pick the workflow → "…" → _Disable workflow_), but I'll plan everything in code so it doesn't depend on that.

## The options, step by step

**Option A: swap labels everywhere**

- _What we do:_ in every workflow file, change `runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest` → `ubuntu-latest` (and similar). Add the guard line to every job that publishes or releases.
- _What you'd see on a PR:_ the checks start within a minute or two.
- _On a future sync:_ any time upstream edits one of those `runs-on:` lines or the lines next to them, git conflicts, and the fix is "keep ours." Worse, when upstream **adds a new job** with `depot-…`, git merges it in quietly with no conflict, and that one job starts hanging again.
- _Size:_ about 38 files edited.

**Option B: our own CI file, upstream's turned off**

- _What we do:_ write one new file, `fork-ci.yml`, that runs lint, typecheck, unit tests and build on `ubuntu-latest`. Then turn off every inherited workflow, either by deleting it or by adding the guard line.
- _What you'd see on a PR:_ one small, fast set of checks that the team fully owns and understands.
- _On a future sync:_ our file never conflicts. The turned-off upstream files still conflict when upstream edits them, through either the guard lines or the deleted files.
- _What we lose:_ E2E browser tests, screenshot tests, and the PR bots, unless we copy them into our file (which is just Option A again).

**Option C: hybrid (still my recommendation)**

- _What we do:_
  1. Swap labels only in the ~6 core PR workflows: `check`, `build`, `e2e-test`, `api-browser-test`, plus the "harmless" bots you chose to keep.
  2. Add the guard line to the Depot test-report steps, so `master` doesn't go red.
  3. Add the guard line to the upstream-only release, publish and scheduled jobs, and to the bots you chose to turn off.
  4. Add a tiny new workflow, `fork-ci-guard.yml`, that searches the workflow files for `depot-` and fails the PR if it finds one in a workflow we want running. This catches the "upstream quietly added a new Depot job" case automatically.
  5. Add a small script someone can run after each sync to redo the label swap in one command.
- _What you'd see on a PR:_ the real checks (lint, typecheck, tests, build, E2E, screenshots) all running. If a sync brings Depot back, the guard check goes red and names the file.
- _On a future sync:_ conflicts are about the same as Option A for the files we touch, but nothing can break silently, and the fix is one command.

**Rejected:** a self-hosted runner (on a public repo it would run any stranger's PR code on your machine) and paying for Depot.

Your other answers are recorded: Linux-only CI scope, and keep only the harmless bots.

# Plan: Make CI actually run on PRs (issue #101)

## Context

All CI in CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget is inherited from upstream `actualbudget/actual`.
Nearly every job requests a **Depot** runner (`runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest`, matrix
`runner: depot-ubuntu-24.04-8`, …). Depot is a paid runner service that upstream pays for; our org has
none, so every job sits at "Waiting for a runner…" until GitHub cancels it (~24h).
The public Actions API confirms every recent run is `queued` or `cancelled`. As a result, lint, typecheck and
test failures have reached `master` uncaught. The repo is public, so GitHub-hosted runners
are free (Linux: 4 vCPU / 16 GB, about the same as `depot-ubuntu-latest-4`).

Hidden traps beyond the runner labels (found during exploration):

- `depot/test-report-action` steps (Depot OIDC) would turn `master` red: check.yml:117 runs on push.
- GitHub reports the repo as `fork: false`, so upstream's `repository.fork` guards don't skip.
  Once runners work, docker-nightly (pushes to ghcr), publish-nightly-electron, npm publish,
  stale (closes our PRs), etc. would **actually run**.

**User decisions:** Option C (hybrid + guard), all done in code (no admin access), disable
via guard lines, Linux-only CI, keep only the harmless bots.

## Approach

### 1. Swap runner labels in workflows we want running

Label map: `depot-ubuntu-latest`, `depot-ubuntu-latest-4` → `ubuntu-latest`;
`depot-ubuntu-24.04-8` → `ubuntu-24.04`; `depot-ubuntu-22.04` → `ubuntu-22.04`.

- Core: `check.yml`, `build.yml` (except `mobile`), `e2e-test.yml` (all jobs incl.
  `functional-desktop-app`, which is Linux in a Playwright container), `api-browser-test.yml`,
  `electron-pr.yml` (Linux matrix entry only; **remove** the windows/macos matrix entries,
  because a job-level `if:` can't see `matrix`).
- Small PR checks: `crdt-version-check`, `news-feed-check`, `docs-spelling`,
  `dependency-review`, `do-not-merge`.
- Kept bots: `ai-generated-label`, `fork-pr-welcome`, `size-compare`, `e2e-vrt-comment`,
  `migration-warnings-comment`, `issues-remove-help-wanted`.

### 2. Guard Depot-only steps and macOS

Prepend `github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual' && ` to the existing `if:` of each
`Report test results to Depot` step (check.yml:119; e2e-test.yml report-e2e / functional-desktop-app /
merge-vrt). Add `if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'` to build.yml `mobile` (macOS).

### 3. Turn off upstream-only workflows with guard lines

Add `if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'` to **every job** (combine with `&&` where an
`if:` exists; leave their `depot-*` labels untouched so the diff stays minimal):

- Turned-off bots: `autofix`, `stale`, `release-notes`, `issues-close-feature-requests`,
  `issues-close-tech-support`, `issues-feature-implemented`, `count-points`,
  `vrt-update-generate`, `vrt-update-apply` (the last two need `ACTIONS_UPDATE_TOKEN`).
- Publish/release: `netlify-release`, `docker-release`, `docker-nightly`, `electron-master`
  (incl. the `ubuntu-latest` create-release job), `publish-nightly-electron`,
  `publish-npm-packages`, `publish-crdt`, `publish-flathub`, `publish-microsoft-store`.
- Already guarded upstream (no change): `cut-release-branch`, `i18n-string-extract-master`,
  `nightly-theme-catalog-scan`, `discord-release-notifications`.

### 4. New fork-owned checker script: `.github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs`

Zero-dependency Node script, placed next to the existing `.github/scripts/count-points.mjs`.

- Scans `.github/workflows/*.yml` line by line. It tracks each job block (2-space key under `jobs:`)
  and treats a job as guarded if its job-level `if:` mentions `github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'`
  or `github.repository_owner == 'actualbudget'`.
- Default (check mode): reports `file:line` for every `depot-*` label (`runs-on:` or matrix `runner:`)
  in an **unguarded** job, with the suggested replacement and a hint ("swap it, or guard
  the job if it's upstream-only"), and exits 1.
- `--fix`: rewrites those labels in place with the label map (text replacement on the reported
  lines only, so formatting and comments are preserved). This is the one-command re-apply after an
  upstream sync.

### 5. New fork-owned workflow: `.github/workflows/fork-ci-guard.yml`

Triggers: `pull_request`, `push` to master. `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, `permissions: contents: read`,
`actions/checkout` pinned to the same SHA the other workflows use, with `persist-credentials: false`
(so zizmor in check.yml passes). One step: `node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs`. There's no yarn
install (Node is preinstalled on the runner), so the run takes seconds.

### 6. Team docs: add a "CI in our fork" section to `STUDENTS.md` (fork-owned)

Explain why we use GitHub-hosted runners, what the guard check means, the sync recipe
("after merging upstream, run `node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --fix`; on
`runs-on:` conflicts keep ours"), which workflows are turned off, and a note that a maintainer with
write/admin access can cancel the ~20 stuck queued runs (otherwise they expire on their own).
This covers acceptance criterion 4.

## Critical files

- Modified: `.github/workflows/{check,build,e2e-test,api-browser-test,electron-pr}.yml`, the
  small-check and kept-bot workflows (label swap), and the guarded workflows listed in step 3.
- New: `.github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs`, `.github/workflows/fork-ci-guard.yml`.
- Docs: `STUDENTS.md`.
- Reused: `.github/actions/setup/action.yml` (already portable, unchanged).

## Verification

1. Locally run `node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs`. It should exit 0. Temporarily
   re-add a `depot-ubuntu-latest` label to an unguarded job: it should exit 1 and report the line.
   Then `--fix` should restore it.
2. Sync simulation: copy the pre-change workflows (`git show 82d9aad19:<file>`) into the scratchpad,
   run `--fix` against the copy, and diff the result against the hand edits from steps 1 and 2. Only the guard
   lines should differ.
3. `grep -rn "depot-" .github/workflows`: every remaining hit is in a guarded job.
4. `yarn lint:fix` on changed files. Commit via the `committing-actual-changes` skill;
   PR title `[AI] Run CI on GitHub-hosted runners (#101)`, template left blank.
5. On the PR itself (`pull_request` runs the PR branch's workflow files), Test, Build, E2E,
   API Browser, Electron (Linux) and Fork CI guard should start within minutes, and the
   upstream-only workflows should show "skipped". Expected, out-of-scope failures: lint (93 files
   on master) and the 6 `mutations.test.tsx` tests; VRT may also fail if snapshots drifted.
6. After merge, the push-to-master Test/Build runs finish with the Depot step skipped,
   and docker-nightly is skipped. size-compare and other `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` bots only take
   effect after merge, because they run the default branch's copy of the workflow.

## Wrap-up

Log the session with SpecStory per the user's instructions (details to come at the end).

install (Node is preinstalled on the runner), so the run takes seconds.

Explain why we use GitHub-hosted runners, what the guard check means, the sync recipe
("after merging upstream, run `node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --fix`; on
`runs-on:` conflicts keep ours"), which workflows are turned off, and a note that a maintainer with
write/admin access can cancel the ~20 stuck queued runs (otherwise they expire on their own).

```mjs
// Fork-only CI guard for CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget (see issue #101).
//
// Upstream (actualbudget/actual) runs its workflows on paid Depot runners
// (`runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest`, ...). Our fork has no Depot account, so any
// job asking for a `depot-*` label sits in the queue until GitHub cancels it.
//
// This script finds every `depot-*` runner label in a job that can run on our
// fork. A job is treated as "upstream-only" (and skipped) when its job-level
// `if:` checks `github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'` or
// `github.repository_owner == 'actualbudget'` without any `||`.
//
// Usage:
//   node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs          # report, exit 1 if any
//   node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --fix    # swap to GitHub runners
//   node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --dir <workflows-dir> [--fix]

import { readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const UPSTREAM_GUARDS = [
  /github\.repository\s*==\s*'actualbudget\/actual'/,
  /github\.repository_owner\s*==\s*'actualbudget'/,
];

// depot-<github label>[-<core count>] -> <github label>
const DEPOT_LABEL =
  /\bdepot-(ubuntu-latest|ubuntu-\d\d\.\d\d(?:-arm)?|windows-\d{4}|macos-(?:latest|\d+))(?:-\d+)?\b/g;
const ANY_DEPOT_LABEL = /\bdepot-[\w.-]+/g;
const RUNNER_LINE = /^\s*(?:-\s+)?(?:runs-on|runner):/;

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const shouldFix = args.includes('--fix');
const dirIndex = args.indexOf('--dir');
const workflowsDir =
  dirIndex === -1
    ? fileURLToPath(new URL('../workflows', import.meta.url))
    : args[dirIndex + 1];

function indentOf(line) {
  return line.length - line.trimStart().length;
}

function isGuarded(ifText) {
  return (
    !ifText.includes('||') && UPSTREAM_GUARDS.some(guard => guard.test(ifText))
  );
}

// Splits a workflow into its jobs: [{ name, start, end, ifText }]
function findJobs(lines) {
  const jobsLine = lines.findIndex(line => /^jobs:\s*(#.*)?$/.test(line));
  if (jobsLine === -1) {
    return [];
  }

  const jobs = [];
  for (let i = jobsLine + 1; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];
    if (line.trim() === '' || line.trimStart().startsWith('#')) {
      continue;
    }
    if (indentOf(line) === 0) {
      break;
    }
    const jobKey = line.match(/^ {2}([\w-]+):\s*(#.*)?$/);
    if (jobKey) {
      if (jobs.length > 0) {
        jobs[jobs.length - 1].end = i;
      }
      jobs.push({ name: jobKey[1], start: i, end: lines.length, ifText: '' });
    }
  }

  for (const job of jobs) {
    for (let i = job.start + 1; i < job.end; i++) {
      if (!/^ {4}if:/.test(lines[i])) {
        continue;
      }
      // Collect multi-line `if:` values (indented deeper than the key)
      const ifLines = [lines[i]];
      for (let j = i + 1; j < job.end; j++) {
        if (lines[j].trim() !== '' && indentOf(lines[j]) <= 4) {
          break;
        }
        ifLines.push(lines[j]);
      }
      job.ifText = ifLines.join('\n');
      break;
    }
  }

  return jobs;
}

const problems = [];
let fixedCount = 0;

const files = readdirSync(workflowsDir)
  .filter(file => /\.ya?ml$/.test(file))
  .sort();

for (const file of files) {
  const path = join(workflowsDir, file);
  const lines = readFileSync(path, 'utf8').split('\n');
  let changed = false;

  for (const job of findJobs(lines)) {
    if (isGuarded(job.ifText)) {
      continue;
    }
    for (let i = job.start + 1; i < job.end; i++) {
      const line = lines[i];
      if (!RUNNER_LINE.test(line)) {
        continue;
      }
      for (const [label] of line.matchAll(ANY_DEPOT_LABEL)) {
        const replacement = label.replace(DEPOT_LABEL, '$1');
        const canFix = replacement !== label;
        if (shouldFix && canFix) {
          continue;
        }
        problems.push(
          `${file}:${i + 1} job "${job.name}" uses ${label}` +
            (canFix
              ? ` (use ${replacement})`
              : ' (no known GitHub equivalent)'),
        );
      }
      if (shouldFix) {
        const fixed = line.replace(DEPOT_LABEL, '$1');
        if (fixed !== line) {
          lines[i] = fixed;
          changed = true;
          fixedCount++;
        }
      }
    }
  }

  if (changed) {
    writeFileSync(path, lines.join('\n'));
  }
}

if (shouldFix) {
  console.log(
    `Swapped ${fixedCount} Depot runner label(s) to GitHub-hosted runners.`,
  );
}

if (problems.length > 0) {
  console.error(
    'These jobs request Depot runners, which our fork does not have, so they\n' +
      'will wait in the queue until GitHub cancels them:\n',
  );
  for (const problem of problems) {
    console.error(`  ${problem}`);
  }
  console.error(
    '\nFix: run `node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --fix` to swap them to\n' +
      'GitHub-hosted runners, or, if the job is upstream-only (publishing,\n' +
      "releases, ...), add `if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'` to it.\n" +
      'See "CI in our fork" in STUDENTS.md.',
  );
  process.exit(1);
}

console.log('No unguarded Depot runner labels found.');
```

```python
"""One-off helper for issue #101: add upstream-only guards to workflow jobs."""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

GUARD = "github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'"
WORKFLOWS = Path(sys.argv[1])

# file -> list of jobs to guard (None = every job in the file)
TARGETS = {
    "autofix.yml": None,
    "stale.yml": None,
    "release-notes.yml": None,
    "issues-close-feature-requests.yml": None,
    "issues-close-tech-support.yml": None,
    "issues-feature-implemented.yml": None,
    "count-points.yml": None,
    "vrt-update-generate.yml": None,
    "vrt-update-apply.yml": None,
    "netlify-release.yml": None,
    "docker-release.yml": None,
    "docker-nightly.yml": None,
    "electron-master.yml": None,
    "publish-nightly-electron.yml": None,
    "publish-npm-packages.yml": None,
    "publish-crdt.yml": None,
    "publish-flathub.yml": None,
    "publish-microsoft-store.yml": None,
    "build.yml": ["mobile"],
}

JOB_KEY = re.compile(r"^  ([\w-]+):\s*(#.*)?$")


def guard_file(path, only_jobs):
    lines = path.read_text().split("\n")
    jobs_line = lines.index("jobs:")
    starts = [i for i in range(jobs_line + 1, len(lines)) if JOB_KEY.match(lines[i])]
    guarded = []
    # Walk backwards so insertions don't shift later job indexes
    for n, start in reversed(list(enumerate(starts))):
        name = JOB_KEY.match(lines[start]).group(1)
        if only_jobs is not None and name not in only_jobs:
            continue
        end = starts[n + 1] if n + 1 < len(starts) else len(lines)
        if_idx = next(
            (i for i in range(start + 1, end) if lines[i].startswith("    if:")), None
        )
        if if_idx is None:
            lines.insert(start + 1, f"    if: {GUARD}")
        else:
            value = lines[if_idx][len("    if:"):].strip()
            if value in (">", ">-", "|", "|-"):
                lines.insert(if_idx + 1, f"      {GUARD} &&")
            elif value.startswith("${{") and value.endswith("}}"):
                inner = value[3:-2].strip()
                lines[if_idx] = f"    if: ${{{{ {GUARD} && ({inner}) }}}}"
            else:
                lines[if_idx] = f"    if: {GUARD} && ({value})"
        guarded.append(name)
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines))
    return list(reversed(guarded))


for file, only_jobs in TARGETS.items():
    print(f"{file}: {', '.join(guard_file(WORKFLOWS / file, only_jobs))}")

```

```yaml
# Fork-only workflow (CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget, issue #101).
#
# Fails when a job that can run on our fork asks for a Depot runner
# (`depot-*`). We have no Depot account, so such jobs would otherwise wait in
# the queue until GitHub cancels them. Upstream syncs can bring these labels
# back; see "CI in our fork" in STUDENTS.md for how to fix them.
name: Fork CI guard

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  runner-labels:
    name: No Depot runner labels
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check workflow runner labels
        run: node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs
```

152	## Contributing workflow
153
154	All team members have write access to this repository, so the team uses a **branch-based** workflow — not forks. Here is the background and the commands.
155
156	**Why not forks?** Forking is the standard model for contributing to open-source projects where you _don't_ have write access: you fork to your own GitHub account, clone your fork, and open a PR from your fork back to the original. You will encounter this when contributing to the upstream project. But for your course team — where everyone has write access to the shared repo — it just adds confusion: two clones on your machine, two remotes to keep in sync, merge conflicts that are harder to reason about.
157
158	**Branch-based workflow** is what most professional teams use internally. You clone the shared repo once, create a short-lived branch for each issue, push the branch back to the same repo, and open a PR from that branch into `main`. One clone, one remote, full PR workflow.
159
160	### For each issue you work on
161
162	```bash
163	# One-time setup: clone the team repo (skip if already done)
164	git clone https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget.git
165	cd actual-budget
166
167	# Before starting each issue: make sure you are on a fresh main
168	git checkout main
169	git pull origin main
170
171	# Create a branch named for the issue
172	git checkout -b feat/issue-17-dark-mode      # new feature
173	git checkout -b fix/issue-42-toast-dismiss   # bug fix
174
175	# ... make your changes, run tests ...
176
177	# Stage and commit
178	git add <the files you changed>
179	git commit -m "feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)"
180
181	# Push the branch to the team repo
182	git push origin feat/issue-17-dark-mode
183	```
184
185	After pushing, GitHub shows a **"Compare & pull request"** banner on the repository page. Click it to open a PR from your branch into `main`. Fill in the description (what changed and why), reference the issue (`Closes #17`), and request a review from a teammate.
186
187	**Branch naming:**
188
189	| Prefix | Use for |
190	|---|---|
191	| `feat/issue-<N>-short-description` | new features |
192	| `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` | bug fixes |
193	| `chore/short-description` | docs, config, dependency updates |
194
195	> ⚠️ **`main` is protected — direct pushes are blocked.** All changes go through a reviewed PR. If you accidentally commit to `main` locally, move your changes to a branch before pushing:
196	>
197	> ```bash
198	> git checkout -b fix/issue-42-my-fix   # create branch from your current state
199	> git checkout main
200	> git reset --hard origin/main          # revert local main to match remote
201	> ```
202
203	**After your PR is merged**, delete the branch to keep the repo tidy:
204
205	```bash
206	git checkout main
207	git pull origin main
208	git branch -d feat/issue-17-dark-mode
209	```

41	}
42
43	// Splits an expression on `&&` / `||` outside of parentheses and quotes
44	function splitTopLevel(expr) {
45	  const parts = [];
46	  let hasOr = false;
47	  let depth = 0;
48	  let inQuote = false;
49	  let current = '';
50	  for (let i = 0; i < expr.length; i++) {
51	    const char = expr[i];
52	    const pair = expr.slice(i, i + 2);
53	    if (char === "'") {
54	      inQuote = !inQuote;
55	    } else if (!inQuote && char === '(') {
56	      depth++;
57	    } else if (!inQuote && char === ')') {
58	      depth--;
59	    } else if (!inQuote && depth === 0 && (pair === '&&' || pair === '||')) {
60	      hasOr ||= pair === '||';

65	    }
66	    current += char;

Both problems are fixed on the branch. Nothing is committed yet.

**1. AI label bot:** it was failing because our repo doesn't have an "AI generated" label (only the four `scope:` labels), so adding it errored on every `[AI]` PR. I turned it off with the same guard line as the other upstream-only bots, and set its runner label back to upstream's so the only difference from upstream is the `if:` line. It's also added to the turned-off list in [STUDENTS.md](STUDENTS.md), with a note that we review AI-generated PRs by hand.

**2. Checker gaps:** you were right that it missed labels. Testing showed that quoted values on a `runs-on:` line were actually caught. What slipped through were:

- a quoted `"runs-on":` key
- a label on the line _after_ `runs-on:`, either as a list item or under `labels:`
- a matrix value under any key other than `runner` (e.g. `os:`)
- flow-style matrix entries like `include: [{ runner: … }]`

It also got two things wrong:

- A quoted job name wasn't recognized as a job, so its label was blamed on the job above it.
- A quoted guard (`if: "github.repository == …"`) wasn't recognized, so a turned-off job was wrongly flagged.

[fork-ci-runners.mjs](.github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs) now checks _every_ non-comment line in a running job for `depot-<label>`, whatever the key or quoting, and it accepts quoted job names and quoted `if:` conditions. A label mentioned only in a comment is ignored, and a `#` inside quotes isn't mistaken for a comment. `--fix` keeps each label's original quotes. The downside is that a stray `depot-` anywhere else in a running job would also be flagged, which should be rare.

**Re-tested:**

- The checker passes on our real workflow files.
- On a test file covering all the spellings above plus the two comment cases, it flags exactly the 11 it should and `--fix` repairs all of them.
- A reintroduced quoted label is caught and fixed.
- The sync simulation still reproduces our branch, apart from the three hand edits.
- `oxfmt` and `oxlint` pass on the changed files.

The question from before still stands: shall I commit and push the branch, so you can open the PR from GitHub and send the SpecStory details?

```mjs
// Fork-only CI guard for CSCI-435-SE/actual-budget (see issue #101).
//
// Upstream (actualbudget/actual) runs its workflows on paid Depot runners
// (`runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest`, ...). Our fork has no Depot account, so any
// job asking for a `depot-*` label sits in the queue until GitHub cancels it.
//
// This script finds every `depot-*` label in a job that can run on our fork.
// It checks the two places a job's runner label comes from: the job's
// `runs-on:` value and its `strategy:` block (matrix values used as
// `runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}`), in any YAML form or quoting. Steps,
// including `run:` scripts, are never checked or changed. Labels that come
// from repo variables (`vars.*`), inputs or other jobs' outputs can't be seen
// here.
//
// A job is treated as "upstream-only" (and skipped) when its job-level `if:`
// is `github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'` (or
// `github.repository_owner == 'actualbudget'`) joined to the rest of the
// condition with `&&`, optionally inside parentheses.
//
// Our fork runs CI on Linux only, so `--fix` only swaps Linux labels. macOS
// and Windows labels are reported for a person to guard or remove.
//
// Usage:
//   node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs          # report, exit 1 if any
//   node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --fix    # swap Linux labels
//   node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --dir <workflows-dir> [--fix]

import { readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const UPSTREAM_GUARD =
  /^(?:github\.repository\s*==\s*'actualbudget\/actual'|github\.repository_owner\s*==\s*'actualbudget')$/;

// depot-<github linux label>[-<core count>] -> <github linux label>
const DEPOT_LINUX_LABEL =
  /\bdepot-(ubuntu-latest|ubuntu-\d\d\.\d\d(?:-arm)?)(?:-\d+)?\b/g;
const DEPOT_NON_LINUX_LABEL = /^depot-(?:macos|windows)/;
const ANY_DEPOT_LABEL = /\bdepot-[\w.-]+/g;
// Job ids and job-level keys, optionally quoted
const JOB_KEY = /^ {2}(['"]?)([\w-]+)\1:\s*(#.*)?$/;
const JOB_IF_KEY = /^ {4}(['"]?)if\1:/;
const JOB_RUNNER_KEY = /^ {4}(['"]?)(?:runs-on|strategy)\1:/;

const args = process.argv.slice(2);
const shouldFix = args.includes('--fix');
const dirIndex = args.indexOf('--dir');
const workflowsDir =
  dirIndex === -1
    ? fileURLToPath(new URL('../workflows', import.meta.url))
    : args[dirIndex + 1];

function indentOf(line) {
  return line.length - line.trimStart().length;
}

// Splits a line into [code, comment], where a YAML comment is a `#` that is
// outside quotes and at the start of the line or after whitespace
function splitComment(line) {
  let quote = null;
  for (let i = 0; i < line.length; i++) {
    const char = line[i];
    if (quote) {
      if (char === quote) {
        quote = null;
      }
    } else if (char === "'" || char === '"') {
      quote = char;
    } else if (char === '#' && (i === 0 || /\s/.test(line[i - 1]))) {
      return [line.slice(0, i), line.slice(i)];
    }
  }
  return [line, ''];
}

// Splits an expression on `&&` / `||` outside of parentheses and quotes
function splitTopLevel(expr) {
  const parts = [];
  let hasOr = false;
  let depth = 0;
  let inQuote = false;
  let current = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < expr.length; i++) {
    const char = expr[i];
    const pair = expr.slice(i, i + 2);
    if (char === "'") {
      inQuote = !inQuote;
    } else if (!inQuote && char === '(') {
      depth++;
    } else if (!inQuote && char === ')') {
      depth--;
    } else if (!inQuote && depth === 0 && (pair === '&&' || pair === '||')) {
      hasOr ||= pair === '||';
      parts.push(current.trim());
      current = '';
      i++;
      continue;
    }
    current += char;
  }
  parts.push(current.trim());
  return { parts, hasOr };
}

// Removes parentheses that wrap the whole expression: `((a && b))` -> `a && b`
function unwrapParens(expr) {
  let result = expr.trim();
  while (result.startsWith('(') && result.endsWith(')')) {
    let depth = 0;
    let inQuote = false;
    let closesAtEnd = true;
    for (let i = 0; i < result.length - 1; i++) {
      const char = result[i];
      if (char === "'") {
        inQuote = !inQuote;
      } else if (!inQuote && char === '(') {
        depth++;
      } else if (!inQuote && char === ')') {
        depth--;
      }
      if (depth === 0) {
        closesAtEnd = false;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (!closesAtEnd) {
      break;
    }
    result = result.slice(1, -1).trim();
  }
  return result;
}

// True if the expression can only be true when the guard is true
function requiresGuard(expr) {
  const { parts, hasOr } = splitTopLevel(unwrapParens(expr));
  if (hasOr) {
    return false;
  }
  return parts.some(
    part =>
      UPSTREAM_GUARD.test(part) || (parts.length > 1 && requiresGuard(part)),
  );
}

function isGuarded(ifText) {
  let expr = ifText
    .replace(/^\s*(['"]?)if\1:\s*([>|][-+]?)?/, '')
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
    .trim();
  // Unwrap a YAML-quoted value: "..." or '...' (with '' as an escaped quote)
  if (/^".*"$/.test(expr)) {
    expr = expr.slice(1, -1);
  } else if (/^'.*'$/.test(expr)) {
    expr = expr.slice(1, -1).replaceAll("''", "'");
  }
  expr = expr.replace(/^\$\{\{(.*)\}\}$/, '$1').trim();
  return requiresGuard(expr);
}

// Lines of a job-level key: the key line plus lines indented deeper than it
function keyBlock(lines, keyLine, end) {
  const block = [keyLine];
  for (let i = keyLine + 1; i < end; i++) {
    if (lines[i].trim() !== '' && indentOf(lines[i]) <= 4) {
      break;
    }
    block.push(i);
  }
  return block;
}

// Splits a workflow into its jobs: [{ name, start, end, ifText, runnerLines }]
function findJobs(lines) {
  const jobsLine = lines.findIndex(line => /^jobs:\s*(#.*)?$/.test(line));
  if (jobsLine === -1) {
    return [];
  }

  const jobs = [];
  for (let i = jobsLine + 1; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];
    if (line.trim() === '' || line.trimStart().startsWith('#')) {
      continue;
    }
    if (indentOf(line) === 0) {
      break;
    }
    const jobKey = line.match(JOB_KEY);
    if (jobKey) {
      if (jobs.length > 0) {
        jobs[jobs.length - 1].end = i;
      }
      jobs.push({
        name: jobKey[2],
        start: i,
        end: lines.length,
        ifText: '',
        runnerLines: [],
      });
    }
  }

  for (const job of jobs) {
    for (let i = job.start + 1; i < job.end; i++) {
      if (JOB_IF_KEY.test(lines[i]) && job.ifText === '') {
        job.ifText = keyBlock(lines, i, job.end)
          .map(index => lines[index])
          .join('\n');
      } else if (JOB_RUNNER_KEY.test(lines[i])) {
        job.runnerLines.push(...keyBlock(lines, i, job.end));
      }
    }
  }

  return jobs;
}

function describe(label) {
  const replacement = label.replace(DEPOT_LINUX_LABEL, '$1');
  if (replacement !== label) {
    return { canFix: true, hint: `use ${replacement}` };
  }
  if (DEPOT_NON_LINUX_LABEL.test(label)) {
    return {
      canFix: false,
      hint: 'our fork runs Linux only: guard the job or remove this matrix entry',
    };
  }
  return { canFix: false, hint: 'no known GitHub equivalent' };
}

const problems = [];
let fixedCount = 0;

const files = readdirSync(workflowsDir)
  .filter(file => /\.ya?ml$/.test(file))
  .sort();

for (const file of files) {
  const path = join(workflowsDir, file);
  const lines = readFileSync(path, 'utf8').split('\n');
  let changed = false;

  for (const job of findJobs(lines)) {
    if (isGuarded(job.ifText)) {
      continue;
    }
    for (const i of job.runnerLines) {
      const [code, comment] = splitComment(lines[i]);
      for (const [label] of code.matchAll(ANY_DEPOT_LABEL)) {
        const { canFix, hint } = describe(label);
        if (shouldFix && canFix) {
          continue;
        }
        problems.push(
          `${file}:${i + 1} job "${job.name}" uses ${label} (${hint})`,
        );
      }
      if (shouldFix) {
        const fixed = code.replace(DEPOT_LINUX_LABEL, '$1');
        if (fixed !== code) {
          lines[i] = fixed + comment;
          changed = true;
          fixedCount++;
        }
      }
    }
  }

  if (changed) {
    writeFileSync(path, lines.join('\n'));
  }
}

if (shouldFix) {
  console.log(
    `Swapped ${fixedCount} Depot runner label(s) to GitHub-hosted Linux runners.`,
  );
}

if (problems.length > 0) {
  console.error(
    'These jobs request Depot runners, which our fork does not have, so they\n' +
      'will wait in the queue until GitHub cancels them:\n',
  );
  for (const problem of problems) {
    console.error(`  ${problem}`);
  }
  console.error(
    '\nFix: run `node .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs --fix` to swap Linux\n' +
      'labels to GitHub-hosted runners. For macOS/Windows jobs, or jobs that are\n' +
      'upstream-only (publishing, releases, ...), add\n' +
      "`if: github.repository == 'actualbudget/actual'` to the job instead.\n" +
      'See "CI in our fork" in STUDENTS.md.',
  );
  process.exit(1);
}

console.log('No unguarded Depot runner labels found.');
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-20 02:09:36Z)**_

All three problems are fixed in the checker script, and none of the workflow files needed to change this round. Nothing is committed yet.

1. **Guards in parentheses:** the checker now unwraps parentheses around the whole condition and looks inside parenthesized `&&` groups. `(guard)`, `((guard)) && x` and `(guard && x) && y` all count as turned off. `(guard || x)`, `(x) || (guard)` and `!(guard)` are still flagged, because those jobs could run on our fork.
2. **macOS/Windows labels:** `--fix` now only swaps Linux labels. macOS and Windows labels stay flagged with "our fork runs Linux only: guard the job or remove this matrix entry". [STUDENTS.md](STUDENTS.md) has a new step 3 for that case.
3. **Labels in shell commands:** the checker now looks only where a runner label can come from: a job's `runs-on:` section and its `strategy:` matrix. Upstream uses only those two. `run:` scripts, step `with:` inputs and `env:` are never checked or changed. Labels set through repo variables, inputs or another job's outputs can't be seen from the files; that limitation is noted in the script's header comment.

- The checker passes on our real workflow files.

5-What is one thing you learned about the codebase or about software engineering practice?
6-- I learned about “Depot” which is what the upstream repository uses to run CI tests. Essentially Depot is a cloud based CI runner that runs extremely fast. It saves the developers a lot of time not having to wait for CI tests to fully run (it can take a while), but it costs money (through tokens) so we’re not able to access their depot. I also learned that with CI testing, you can run the CI test as if the code were running on a Linux machine, that way if you have one developer working on Mac and another on Windows, their operating system won’t interfere with the running of the checks. This ensures that the code works regardless of the operating system and hardware.

# Committing Changes in actualbudget/actual

Before creating any git commit or pull request in this repo, read:

**`.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md`**

It is the authoritative source for the rules you must apply yourself: the `[AI]` PR-title prefix and leaving the PR template blank (and the Chinese exception). The mechanical commit/git rules are enforced by tooling and aren't restated there. Read it on every commit/PR session so any updates are picked up automatically.

## The one rule worth restating

Every commit message and every pull request title MUST begin with `[AI]`. Commit messages are checked by the git-guard hook (a missing prefix is blocked before the commit lands), so the one that needs _your_ attention is the PR title — nothing checks it for you, and the cost of forgetting it is high since the PR has to be renamed by hand. Examples:

- `[AI] Fix type error in account validation` — correct
- `Fix type error in account validation` — wrong, missing prefix

The PR-template rule and the rest live in the rules file. Read it before each commit/PR rather than relying on this skill's summary, because the rules file evolves and this skill deliberately does not restate it.

## Why this matters

Maintainers triage AI-authored contributions separately, and the `[AI]` prefix is what makes that triage fast — it also drives the automatic `"AI generated"` PR label, so getting the prefix right is the one action that gates the whole triage path. Without it the PR looks like a normal human contribution and the wrong review process gets applied. The "do not fill in the PR template" rule exists because the human is the one who actually tested the change and can write the Description / Testing / Checklist sections honestly — an AI-filled template misrepresents who did what.

The rules file is short. Read it.

ARGUMENTS: Two commits on branch fix/issue-101-ci-runners: (1) CI changes for issue #101 (workflows, .github/scripts/fork-ci-runners.mjs, STUDENTS.md), (2) AI log ai-logs/sprint2/tigerk9/2026-10-20_claude-code_issue-101-ci-runners.md. Then push.
